Freedom 250 · Crypto · Reference · Crypto overview

The rules: who is allowed to do what, and is it law yet?

This page reads every rule the library holds on U.S. crypto in one walk: the GENIUS Act (enacted July 18, 2025) and its 28 dated steps, 14 of them proposals not yet final; the 8 other crypto rules, orders and bills and where each stands; the Crypto Hub's nine-step legal process walk with its 7 worked cases and qualification records; the SEC's custody proposal provision by provision (36 provisions, all 760 pages and 342 comment questions); the CFTC's 30-provision baseline; the SEC's Innovation Exemption (12 conditions, 15 clocks); the Federal Reserve Board's two GENIUS proposals; and 9 other jurisdictions' laws. A proposal grants no permission to anyone until it is final.

    Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act)Law

    Enacted: 2025-07-18 · Also shown on: GENIUS Act timeline
    Public law
    Pub. L. 119-27
    Enacted
    2025-07-18
    Effective date rule
    The Act takes effect on the earlier of January 18, 2027 (18 months after enactment) or 120 days after the primary regulators issue final implementing rules. No final rule existed by September 20, 2026 (120 days before January 18, 2027), so any later final rule lands after January 18 and the effective date is January 18, 2027.
    Sources: govinfo.gov

    Answered: Has any agency issued a final rule?Answered in the saved record

    Answer evidence through: 2026-10-21
    Answer
    Yes. The OCC released its final issuer rule on October 21, 2026, effective January 18, 2027. At the saved October 21 release snapshot, application and transition-waiver intake still awaited OMB paperwork approval and a separate OCC opening notice.

    Agency release, Federal Register publication, effective date, intake opening and issuer approval remain distinct.

    Existing saved owner answer replaces the stale open-question status; no new agency-wide search or collection-clock refresh.

    What the Act's provisions say, in plain words

    · 6 rows

    Read from: _Workspace/Indexes/masters/stablecoins.json › law_context

    who-may-issue

    Evidence through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: What does the GENIUS Act say about issuers, reserves and holder rights?
    Provision
    Sec. 3(a); Sec. 2(23); Sec. 2(11)
    Plain words
    Only a 'permitted payment stablecoin issuer' may issue a payment stablecoin in the United States. That means a U.S.-formed company that is (A) an approved subsidiary of an insured bank, (B) a federal qualified issuer (a nonbank or uninsured national bank approved by the OCC), or (C) a state qualified issuer.
    Quote
    It shall be unlawful for any person other than a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to issue a payment stablecoin in the United States. (Sec. 3(a))
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Sources: GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18)

    definition

    Evidence through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: What does the GENIUS Act say about issuers, reserves and holder rights?
    Provision
    Sec. 2(22)
    Plain words
    A digital asset used or designed for payment or settlement whose issuer is obligated to convert, redeem or repurchase it for a fixed amount of money and promises (or creates a reasonable expectation of) a stable value. National currencies, bank deposits and securities are excluded.
    Quote
    does not include a digital asset that— (i) is a national currency; (ii) is a deposit ...; (iii) is a security ... (Sec. 2(22)(B))
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Sources: GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18)

    reserves

    Evidence through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: What does the GENIUS Act say about issuers, reserves and holder rights?
    Provision
    Sec. 4(a)(1)(A)(i)-(viii); Sec. 4(a)(2); Sec. 4(a)(1)(C); Sec. 4(a)(3)(A)
    Plain words
    At least 1:1 reserves limited to: U.S. coins and currency; demand deposits; Treasury bills, notes or bonds with 93 days or less to maturity; money received under repurchase agreements backed by such Treasury bills; overnight reverse repurchase agreements collateralized by Treasuries; shares of registered government money market funds investing in these; other similarly liquid federal government assets the regulator approves; and tokenized forms of these. Reserves may not be pledged, rehypothecated or reused except in narrow cases. The issuer must publish its reserve composition monthly, and the month-end report must be examined by a registered public accounting firm.
    Quote
    Reserves required under paragraph (1)(A) may not be pledged, rehypothecated, or reused (Sec. 4(a)(2))
    Uncertainty
    Clause (vi) is summarized from the quoted fragment 'securities issued by an investment company registered under section 8(a) of the Investment Company Act of 1940'; the full limits on which funds qualify were not re-read in this pass.
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Sources: GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18)

    interest-ban

    Evidence through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: What does the GENIUS Act say about issuers, reserves and holder rights?
    Provision
    Sec. 4(a)(11)
    Plain words
    Neither a permitted issuer nor a foreign issuer may pay a holder any form of interest or yield, in cash, tokens or anything else, solely for holding, using or keeping the coin. The ban names issuers; it does not name exchanges or other distributors. The OCC's March 2, 2026 proposed rule (not final) would presume the issuer is paying holders when it has an arrangement with an affiliate or related third party that pays them (proposed 12 CFR 15.10(c)(4), 91 FR 10202).
    Quote
    No permitted payment stablecoin issuer or foreign payment stablecoin issuer shall pay the holder of any payment stablecoin any form of interest or yield (whether in cash, tokens, or other consideration) solely in connection with the holding, use, or retention of such payment stablecoin. (Sec. 4(a)(11))
    Uncertainty
    Whether the OCC presumption is rebuttable, and exactly how 'related third party' is defined, were not fully read; the CLARITY market-structure bill's reward limits have not become law.
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Sources: GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · OCC proposed GENIUS rule (91 FR 10202), proposed 12 CFR 15.10(c)(4) (2026-03-02)

    lawful-orders

    Evidence through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: What does the GENIUS Act say about issuers, reserves and holder rights?
    Provision
    Sec. 2(16)(A); Sec. 4(a)(6)(B); Sec. 3(b)(2); Sec. 8(a)(1)
    Plain words
    A 'lawful order' is one that requires a person to seize, freeze, burn or prevent the transfer of payment stablecoins it issued. A permitted issuer may issue only if it has the technical ability to comply with such orders. A foreign issuer's coin may be offered in the U.S. only if the issuer can and will comply with lawful orders.
    Quote
    requires a person to seize, freeze, burn, or prevent the transfer of payment stablecoins issued by the person (Sec. 2(16)(A))
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Sources: GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18)

    platform-cutoff-and-size

    Evidence through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: What does the GENIUS Act say about issuers, reserves and holder rights?
    Provision
    Sec. 3(b)(1); Sec. 4(d)
    Plain words
    Starting three years after enactment (July 18, 2028), a digital-asset service provider may not offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States unless a permitted issuer issued it (foreign issuers have a separate route). A state qualified issuer that passes the $10 billion outstanding threshold must move to the federal framework within 360 days unless its regulator grants a waiver.
    Quote
    beginning on the date that is 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, it shall be unlawful for a digital asset service provider to offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States, unless the payment stablecoin is issued by a permitted payment stablecoin issuer (Sec. 3(b)(1), assembled from quoted fragments)
    Uncertainty
    The $10 billion figure is from the library's July 2026 cards; the fetched text of Sec. 4(d) referred to 'such threshold' without the number being quoted back. The foreign-issuer comparability provision is cited by the library as 12 U.S.C. 5916; its section number in the Act was not confirmed here. The Act's general effective date is kept in the genius_act_milestones master (January 18, 2027).
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Sources: GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18)

    3 · The legal process walk (Crypto Hub legal-process room)

    The nine steps from a claimed right to a repairable result

    · 9 rows

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/TOKENIZATION_ENTITY_RELATIONSHIP_REGISTRY_2026-09-01.json › legal_process_hub.steps

    Name the claim

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    What right is being created, transferred, pledged, redeemed, or paid?
    Explanation
    Start with the instrument and obligation. A share, entitlement, bank deposit, token, collateral interest, and payment instruction carry different rights and obligors.
    Actors
    Issuer or obligor; holder; intermediary.
    Required evidence
    Instrument terms; named obligor; holder-rights description; governing-law clause.
    Output
    A statement of who owes what to whom under which terms.
    Boundary
    Technical possession or a token transfer is not a complete description of legal ownership or discharge.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · SEC Release 34-106246 / S7-2026-30 (2026-09-01) · USDC Terms (2026-09-01)

    Draw the actor perimeter

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    Which legal entity performs each function?
    Explanation
    Separate parent, regulated subsidiary, depository, clearing agency, bank, transfer agent, wallet provider, network, and vendor. One organization can wear several hats; each has separate duties.
    Actors
    Legal operator; regulated subsidiary; service provider; supervisor.
    Required evidence
    Entity chart; registration or charter; service agreement; supervisory route.
    Output
    A role map for issuer, recordkeeper, operator, cash obligor, risk manager, and remedy authority.
    Boundary
    A shared brand, partnership, or technology stack does not merge legal entities or permissions.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · SEC clearing-agency registration overview · Designated_fmu_about.htm

    Establish permission

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    What allows this entity to perform this function now?
    Explanation
    Match the activity to a live authority: terms, registration, operating circular, rulebook, designation, order, exemption, or no-action position. Keep scope and effective date attached.
    Actors
    Regulator; registered intermediary; operator; participant.
    Required evidence
    Statute or regulation; registration/order/letter; effective rulebook; scope and expiry terms.
    Output
    A permission statement with its date, product, participant, and volume limits.
    Boundary
    A proposal, pilot, announcement, or generic FMI label grants no unlisted permission.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · Title VIII — FMU definitions · Regulation HH — scope

    Identify the authoritative record

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    If books disagree, which record decides the holder, balance, or obligation?
    Explanation
    Issuer registers, transfer-agent files, depository entitlement books, bank accounts, and networks can each describe a different legal relationship. Identify the controlling record for this issue and event.
    Actors
    Issuer; recordkeeping transfer agent; depository; bank; network operator.
    Required evidence
    Recordkeeping agreement; record clause; reconciliation design; correction rights.
    Output
    A record hierarchy and named reconciliation point.
    Boundary
    A distributed ledger can be linked to a master file without becoming the legal register for every asset on it.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · SEC Release 34-106246 / S7-2026-30 (2026-09-01) · Ea026411904ex10 9.htm

    Bind the instruction

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    Who may send, validate, and delegate an instruction?
    Explanation
    A valid instruction has an authorized sender, authentication, eligibility checks, and rules for rejection, cancellation, queueing, and delegation.
    Actors
    Customer or participant; bank or broker; operator; technology provider.
    Required evidence
    Access agreement; authentication rules; instruction lifecycle; vendor-control terms.
    Output
    A trace from mandate to accepted instruction, including who can stop it before execution.
    Boundary
    A transmitted message, signed wallet action, or broadcast transaction is not necessarily accepted or irrevocable.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · 010526 operating circular 6 · SWIFT operator and governance roles (2026-09-09)

    Clear the obligation and assemble resources

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    Who matches, nets, collateralizes, funds, or guarantees it?
    Explanation
    Some routes pass instructions onward; others create CCP obligations, prefunded positions, or bank-credit exposure. Map margin, collateral, liquidity, netting, and default resources.
    Actors
    CCP; clearing member; settlement bank; liquidity provider; collateral manager.
    Required evidence
    Clearing rules; margin/liquidity rules; funding-account terms; default waterfall.
    Output
    A resources map of gross and net obligation, pledged resources, funding source, and residual exposure.
    Boundary
    Fast execution or a smaller net payment does not prove liquidity, collateral, or default exposure disappeared.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · PFMI liquidity-risk principles (2026-09-10) · CHIPS rules and disclosures (2026-09-10)

    Settle each leg and name finality

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    What asset moves, in which accounts, and when is each obligation final?
    Explanation
    Securities delivery, cash posting, token transfer, payout, and redemption can have different finality points. Name whether the event is technical confirmation, book-entry posting, contractual discharge, or statutory finality.
    Actors
    Settlement operator; depository; bank; cash issuer; participant.
    Required evidence
    Settlement rule; cash-asset identity; account-entry timing; finality and insolvency clause.
    Output
    A two-leg settlement receipt with named assets, timestamps, and finality rules.
    Boundary
    A confirmed ledger event does not prove the other leg, legal discharge, redemption, or bank availability.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · Fedwire Securities — OC 7 · PFMI liquidity-risk principles (2026-09-10)

    Post, reconcile and service

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    Which books update, and who administers rights after settlement?
    Explanation
    Completion creates customer, participant, depository, transfer-agent, issuer, and sometimes network postings. Servicing covers distributions, votes, corporate actions, maturity, redemption, and reporting.
    Actors
    Recordkeeper; custodian; issuer; administrator; participant.
    Required evidence
    Posting records; reconciliation schedule; servicing agreement; exception reports.
    Output
    A reconciled record chain and named administrator for ongoing holder rights.
    Boundary
    A transaction receipt does not prove all books reconciled or later servicing occurred.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · SEC Release 34-106246 / S7-2026-30 (2026-09-01)

    Repair, allocate loss and prove the result

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How do you trace a financial claim from its legal basis to correction and loss?
    Question
    Who can correct an error, what happens on default or outage, and what proves performance?
    Explanation
    A durable process names correction powers, reversals, disputes, collateral realization, loss allocation, recovery, and wind-down. Separate written controls from observed stress.
    Actors
    Operator; supervisor; default manager; service provider; affected holder.
    Required evidence
    Correction rule; default/recovery plan; loss-allocation rule; incident or stress record.
    Output
    A remedy map naming actor, loss bearer, and evidence level.
    Boundary
    Immutability or a service promise does not remove insolvency, correction, or loss-allocation questions.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · SEC recovery and wind-down final rule (2024-11-18) · PFMI liquidity-risk principles (2026-09-10)

    Seven worked cases, step by step

    Linked electronic securities records

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How does the legal trace differ across seven worked financial cases?, Rule status
    Step: Name the claim
    A security issue and holder right remain the starting legal object. Still open: Specific issue terms are not supplied by the proposal.
    Step: Draw the actor perimeter
    One registered recordkeeping transfer agent would remain accountable. Still open: Each linked-system vendor contract needs review.
    Step: Establish permission
    Release 34-106246/S7-2026-30 was proposed. Still open: No final rule or compliance date at cutoff.
    Step: Identify the authoritative record
    A master file could span linked systems while the transfer agent retains exclusive control. Still open: Actual reconciliation is issue-specific.
    Step: Bind the instruction
    Transfer-agent controls would govern record updates. Still open: No universal wallet or chain instruction rule.
    Step: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
    The proposal itself supplies no clearing or funding arrangement. Still open: Identify the resources required by the actual transaction.
    Step: Settle each leg and name finality
    A chain event could form part of recordkeeping. Still open: It would not itself establish DvP or legal title finality for every issue.
    Step: Post, reconcile and service
    The accountable transfer agent would maintain the master file. Still open: Servicing terms remain issue-specific.
    Step: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
    Named legal responsibility would remain with the transfer agent. Still open: Existing duties, proposed changes and actual provider remedies require separate review.
    Status
    Proposed SEC architecture; not operative law at saved cutoff.
    Summary
    The SEC proposal would accommodate linked electronic systems, including a blockchain or DLT component, while one registered recordkeeping transfer agent retains responsibility and exclusive control of the master securityholder file.
    Boundary
    It would not authorize every chain, bridge, wallet, or vendor as a transfer agent, clearing agency, or FMI.
    Sources: FMI applicability and transfer-agent connection (Read the full saved research: Financial market infrastructure: entity applicability and the transfer-agent connection; research notes) (2026-09-10) · SEC Release 34-106246 / S7-2026-30 (2026-09-01)

    SEC crypto-asset classification and investment-contract FAQs

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How does the legal trace differ across seven worked financial cases?, Rule status
    Step: Name the claim
    Asset classification uses the Commission's definitions of functional and decentralized, while fulfillment of essential-managerial-effort promises uses the functionality or decentralization threshold the issuer itself represented. Still open: An exact asset still needs current system facts, rights and value-source evidence; satisfying an issuer-authored milestone does not itself establish the Commission's classification test.
    Step: Draw the actor perimeter
    The relevant actors include the issuer, affiliates, agents, any Rule 405 promoter, a successor assuming promises, a receipt issuer or custodian and a protocol-based liquid-staking provider. Still open: A brand, developer, platform or successor label does not establish the exact legal relationship or promoter status.
    Step: Establish permission
    The FAQs are issued staff guidance applying Release 33-11412/34-105020 and cite the Commission view in the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets release. Still open: They do not amend the interpretation, make Rule 400 or Form TR operative, approve an offering or grant any intermediary permission.
    Step: Identify the authoritative record
    A pure receipt evidences the depositor's continuing ownership of a stated deposited asset without changing its rights or adding separate economics. Still open: Verify deposit and ownership records, exact token terms, reward source, liens and whether the issuer can transfer, lend, pledge, rehypothecate or otherwise use the asset.
    Step: Bind the instruction
    Marketing current utility and indefinite non-profit-focused aspirations likely do not, without more, promise essential managerial efforts; listing alone does not make a platform a promoter absent Rule 405. Still open: Review the full communication channel, authorization, specificity, profit framing and platform relationship rather than relying on labels.
    Step: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
    A qualifying receipt leaves the issuer unable to use or expose the deposited asset to third-party claims; post-functional buyback announcements are not managerial promises merely because they alter supply. Still open: Custody, balance-sheet use, insolvency exposure, funding source, pool economics and any pre-functional yield or return framing remain transaction-specific.
    Step: Settle each leg and name finality
    The FAQs classify relationships and promises; they do not identify settlement assets, discharge rules, finality or failed-leg treatment. Still open: Every securities, crypto, receipt and cash leg still requires its own account, custody, finality and insolvency analysis.
    Step: Post, reconcile and service
    Once a system is functional, securing, maintaining, improving or enhancing it and facilitating network effects do not involve essential managerial efforts under the cited Commission view. Still open: Separate ordinary post-functional service from unfulfilled issuer promises, new profit-linked undertakings and the actual administration of holder rights.
    Step: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
    Successor assumption preserves the promise relationship; by contrast, issuer statements likely do not create a new investment contract once a functional system has no central party capable of controlling success or failure. Still open: Prove the succession instrument, remaining obligations, control distribution, abandonment or completion facts and any later promise rather than treating a handoff or decentralization slogan as dispositive.
    Status
    Corporation Finance staff guidance issued September 25, 2026; nonbinding and not Commission action.
    Summary
    Nine staff answers apply the March Commission interpretation to two functionality clocks, staking receipts, pure-receipt ownership and no-rehypothecation conditions, utility marketing, successor promises, post-functional development, central-party absence, buybacks and secondary-platform promoter status.
    Boundary
    The FAQs refine legal analysis but create no rule, registration, exemption, safe harbor, venue permission, asset approval or operating receipt. The March interpretation remains the Commission-level object, and Regulation Crypto Assets remains proposed.
    Sources: SEC Corporation Finance crypto-asset FAQs (2026-09-25)

    SEC adviser and regulated-fund crypto custody proposal

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How does the legal trace differ across seven worked financial cases?, Rule status
    Step: Name the claim
    Custody scope depends on the crypto asset's legal classification and account type; self-custody would also require a written Article 8 financial-asset and securities-intermediary election. Still open: Determine the exact asset, account, client right, obligor, governing law and whether the mandatory entitlement frame matches the intended holding relationship.
    Step: Draw the actor perimeter
    Adviser, designated supervised key holders, regulated-fund board, independent accountant, qualified custodian, State trust company, technology provider, client and regulator retain distinct functions. Still open: Prove each legal entity, related-person status, delegation, vendor access, board role and contract rather than using a shared brand or wallet label.
    Step: Establish permission
    Proposed rules 223-1(b)(7), 17f-8 and 17f-9 would create residual self-custody and conditional State trust company routes; self-custody would require a written no-qualified-custodian determination re-tested at least quarterly. Still open: Federal Register publication, final action, effective and compliance dates, asset eligibility, exact custodian availability and route-specific compliance remain unproved.
    Step: Identify the authoritative record
    Required crypto records could be maintained onchain only when true, accurate, current, retained, promptly produced in human-readable form and supplemented offchain for ownership, identity or other missing information. Still open: Name the authoritative record for ownership, customer positions, accounting, statements, correction and disputes; a public address or explorer is not automatically complete.
    Step: Bind the instruction
    Possession of any portion of key materials can establish custody; only designated supervised persons may hold keys and at least two people, including management, must jointly authorize movement. Still open: Inspect the actual MPC or multisignature design, recovery shares, limits, client access, vendor access, authentication and accepted-instruction lifecycle.
    Step: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
    Per-client address segregation, State trust financial statements, internal control reports, network reconciliation and related-cash limits would create a custody protection layer. Still open: Capital, insurance, collateral, liquidity, indemnity, rehypothecation, platform prefunding and default resources remain arrangement-specific or open for comment.
    Step: Settle each leg and name finality
    The proposal recognizes network records and custody controls but does not propose a general exception for assets held on non-custodian trading platforms and does not create a universal DeFi route. Still open: Prove venue authority, cash leg, delivery-versus-payment, technical confirmation, legal discharge, staking or protocol control and finality for each leg.
    Step: Post, reconcile and service
    Addresses, balances, transactions, client statements or electronic views, Article 8 agreements, annual reviews, board records and independent reports would form a joined but multi-record custody constitution. Still open: Corporate actions, airdrops, staking, privacy data, accounting entries, tax, long-term access and reconciliation exceptions still require exact operating evidence.
    Step: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
    The proposal would require cyber response and recovery, board notice for serious events, control-report exceptions, transition to a newly available custodian and an Article 8 creditor-priority frame. Still open: Actual reversibility, insurance payment, insolvency priority, protocol loss, key compromise, custodian failure, client compensation and Commission loss reporting remain unproved or unresolved.
    Status
    Commission proposal issued October 1, 2026; not final, effective, compliant or operating.
    Summary
    The 760-page proposal would create asset-specific adviser self-custody only while no qualified custodian will maintain the covered asset, add a conditional State trust company route, apply fund-board oversight, treat key possession as custody, require segregation, joint authorization, cybersecurity, independent control reporting and Article 8 treatment, and permit qualifying onchain regulatory records with examiner-readable offchain completion.
    Boundary
    The proposal grants no present permission, does not cover every crypto asset or account, supplies no general exchange-custody or DeFi exception, does not make a chain the universal ownership record and does not prove a named adviser, fund, custodian, asset, wallet, protocol or transaction complies or operates.
    Sources: SEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules proposal (2026-10-01) · SEC crypto-custody rulemaking page (2026-10-01) · SEC crypto-custody proposal full-release reading and control crosswalk (Read the full saved research: SEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Crypto Custody Proposal — October 1, 2026; research notes) (2026-10-01)

    CLARITY Act EHF26724 proposed market structure

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How does the legal trace differ across seven worked financial cases?, Rule status
    Step: Name the claim
    Network-token and ancillary-asset provisions would create new federal classification and disclosure branches for some digital-asset transactions. Still open: Enactment, implementing rules and product-specific facts remain necessary; the draft does not classify every existing Hub asset.
    Step: Draw the actor perimeter
    The draft separates SEC/Treasury, banking-agency and CFTC functions and adds activity-based controlled-DeFi tests plus explicit vertically integrated affiliate controls. Still open: Each named legal entity, affiliate link and control fact must still be proved; a brand or protocol label is not the regulated person.
    Step: Establish permission
    Spot exchanges, brokers, dealers, custodians and persons controlling covered DeFi functions would receive proposed registration or compliance routes after the required rules. Still open: EHF26724 is not law, its amendment fields remain blank, and no Hub actor receives a current registration, exemption or charter power from it.
    Step: Identify the authoritative record
    Customer-property, segregation, custody, disclosure and books-and-records provisions would add qualification requirements by intermediary function. Still open: The draft does not make a blockchain the authoritative legal record for every asset or replace issue-specific contracts and record hierarchies.
    Step: Bind the instruction
    Revised developer protections would expressly cover specified non-controlling development, validation, node, oracle, bandwidth and user-controlled wallet activities for named money-transmission categories. Still open: The shield is proposed and function-specific, removes the earlier express 18 U.S.C. 1960 reference, and does not create a derivatives or general-conduct immunity.
    Step: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
    Stablecoin rewards would carry a contingent Treasury deposit-flight circuit breaker, while federal and insured credit unions would gain express parity for otherwise-authorized DLT and digital-asset activity. Still open: No deposit flight has been determined, no circuit-breaker rule exists, and asset, liquidity, reserve, credit and balance-sheet exposure remain arrangement-specific.
    Step: Settle each leg and name finality
    The proposal regulates intermediary and customer-protection functions without declaring technical confirmation a universal legal-finality event. Still open: Payment, securities, digital-commodity, custody and insolvency rules still determine finality for each leg and legal relationship.
    Step: Post, reconcile and service
    Registration, customer-property, disclosure and reporting provisions would add function-specific recordkeeping and servicing duties. Still open: Issuer, transfer-agent, custodian, exchange, broker, bank and network records remain separate and would require implementing rules and contracts.
    Step: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
    The draft adds affiliate-conflict controls, exchange proprietary-trading limits, preserved state consumer-protection routes and a permanent ethics enforcement regime with specified federal and state remedies. Still open: These are proposed duties, not present findings that a named Hub company or official complied, violated, caused harm or bears a particular loss.
    Status
    Sponsors' final draft released September 14, 2026; not filed substitute text or operative law.
    Summary
    The 635-page draft retains four divisions and would create coordinated SEC, Treasury, banking-agency and CFTC routes for digital assets, spot intermediaries and controlled DeFi. It adds affiliate-conflict and proprietary-trading controls, a stablecoin deposit-flight circuit breaker, credit-union parity, revised developer protections and a permanent digital-asset ethics regime.
    Boundary
    This case changes future qualification questions only. It grants no present permission, classification, registration or compliance status to any Hub actor, asset, protocol or transaction.
    Sources: CLARITY Act EHF26724 — sponsors' final draft (2026-09-14) · Lummis, Boozman and Scott release final CLARITY Act text (2026-09-14) · CLARITY Act EHF26724 structure, draft delta and Crypto Hub overlay (Read the full saved research: CLARITY Act EHF26724 — Structure, Draft Delta and Crypto Hub Overlay; research notes) (2026-09-14)

    Tokenized NMS Stock Innovation Exemption

    Home checked through: 2026-10-01 · Also shown on: How does the legal trace differ across seven worked financial cases?, Rule status
    Step: Name the claim
    The pool must contain Tokenized NMS Stock carrying the same company interest, voting, dividend and residual rights as the underlying NMS stock. Still open: An actual issue, tokenizer, holder-rights instrument and Securities Act route must still be identified. Synthetic exposures, rights and warrants are outside the defined stock category.
    Step: Draw the actor perimeter
    The order separates the TSV operator, affiliates, tokenizers, liquidity providers, participants, registered activities and service providers and requires public conflict disclosure. Still open: No Hub company or ecosystem is named as a TSV, Covered Firm, tokenizer, participant or service provider. Each legal entity and role must be proved from the eventual notice and contracts.
    Step: Establish permission
    The Commission order is effective and supplies two temporary conditional exemptions through September 17, 2031. Still open: No venue may operate until its complete public notice has run for at least 30 calendar days. Existing broker-dealer and other participant obligations are not broadly waived.
    Step: Identify the authoritative record
    Token holders must receive equivalent stock rights and the TSV must disclose the tokenization, legal and technical evaluation, wallets, chain, contracts, keys and correction-related controls. Still open: The order does not make the AMM, wallet or chain the issuer's authoritative ownership record or grant transfer-agent relief. The actual record hierarchy remains issue-specific.
    Step: Bind the instruction
    Participant access is permissioned even though the application must be public and deployed on public, permissionless DLT. The TSV sets admission standards, pool parameters and administrative controls. Still open: The first notice must identify identity checks, differentiated treatment, upgrade, pause, override, privacy, MEV and service-provider controls. Public infrastructure does not mean public market access.
    Step: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
    A Covered Firm may provide own-account Tokenized NMS Stock liquidity and disclose agreements, fees, rebates and token incentives. The TSV itself may not finance purchases or lend, borrow or hypothecate assets on the venue. Still open: The order supplies no CCP, custody, external financing, haircut, default waterfall or token-inventory receipt. Persistent net XRP or other token inventory remains unproved.
    Step: Settle each leg and name finality
    The order permits a venue architecture capable of self-custody, extended hours and faster settlement and requires disclosure of actual clearing and settlement arrangements. Still open: Near-instant settlement is a possible benefit, not a required or proven legal-finality result. Each securities, crypto, money-market-fund and cash leg needs its own finality and insolvency analysis.
    Step: Post, reconcile and service
    The TSV must retain detailed interest, execution, permissioning, wallet, fee, halt, ADV, notice and event records; equivalent voting, dividend and issuer-communication rights must continue. Still open: Trade reporting within ten minutes is not the same as SIP reporting or proof that issuer, transfer-agent, custodian and participant books reconciled. Corporate-action servicing remains product-specific.
    Step: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
    Underlying-market halts must carry across; significant operational events require participant and SEC notice and remediation; records remain examinable by the Commission. Still open: The order can require disclosure that surveillance, complaint or other protections are absent. It does not itself provide a complete customer-loss, clearing-default, custody-failure or smart-contract remedy.
    Status
    Effective SEC exemptive order through September 17, 2031; no operating TSV established at the saved cutoff.
    Summary
    Release 34-106402 conditionally exempts a Tokenized Securities Venue from the Exchange Act definition of exchange and a qualifying own-account AMM liquidity provider from the dealer definition. Permissioned pools must use auditable public applications deployed on public, permissionless DLT; at least one leg must be Tokenized NMS Stock, and the other may be another such stock, any non-security crypto asset or a tokenized money market fund.
    Boundary
    The order opens a venue category, not a named venue, chain, token or product. A complete TSV notice must run for at least 30 calendar days, and issuer, issuance, record, custody, clearing, settlement, participant and failure rules remain separate.
    Sources: SEC Release 34-106402 — Tokenized NMS Stock Innovation Exemption (2026-09-17) · SEC Tokenized NMS Stock Innovation Exemption — full order analysis (Read the full saved research: SEC Tokenized NMS Stock Innovation Exemption; research notes) (2026-09-17)

    Three visual cases: asset, money and record lanes

    · 3 rows

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/TOKENIZATION_ENTITY_RELATIONSHIP_REGISTRY_2026-09-01.json › qualifications.visual_cases

    BUIDL · subscribe and record fund shares

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: BUIDL
    Description
    Follow the fund share, subscription money and official register. This maps contractual responsibilities; individual payment receipts remain unresolved.
    Stages
    • Title: Eligible offering access · Lanes: Asset: Text: BUIDL is offered through the named placement and access function for eligible investors.; Boundary: Product-specific eligibility and offering restrictions remain controlling; placement authority is not transfer-agent authority.; Status: documented; Money: Text: The payment instruction, bank, funding account, and receipt for a particular subscription are not mapped.; Boundary: The saved BUIDL records do not establish a subscription-payment route or completed cash posting.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Eligibility to enter an offering is documented separately from the shareholder record.; Boundary: Admission does not by itself establish a recorded fund-share entitlement.; Status: documented
    • Title: Fund-share issuance and control book · Lanes: Asset: Text: The fund issuer creates shares; Securitize acts under its appointment.; Boundary: Manager, fund, and transfer agent are separate persons and systems.; Status: documented; Money: Text: Issuance requires confirmation of receipt or credit of subscription funds to the custodian.; Boundary: Contractual condition in section 2.3; a particular investor’s payment receipt is not provided.; Status: documented; Record: Text: Securitize maintains the issuer’s share register.; Boundary: The control book is distinct from a wallet, bridge, or chain consensus record.; Status: documented
    • Title: Named network representation · Lanes: Asset: Text: BUIDL has named live representations on supported networks, including Ethereum.; Boundary: Network availability is not proof that a network is the exclusive or legally authoritative register.; Status: documented; Money: Text: No network representation establishes a subscription payment or cash settlement path.; Boundary: The saved evidence does not link the representation to a particular money movement.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Securitize's multichain model uses Wormhole infrastructure while the regulated control book remains external to transport.; Boundary: Transport does not replace the transfer-agent record or determine legal title.; Status: documented
    • Title: Servicing and correction · Lanes: Asset: Text: Ongoing BUIDL share servicing remains governed by the reviewed transfer-agent agreement.; Boundary: The terms and required instructions determine whether a transfer is recognized.; Status: documented; Money: Text: Cash redemption route and payout completion for this case are not documented here.; Boundary: The case does not treat a separate RLUSD exchange option as a subscription or fiat-payout proof.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Securitize may refuse a transfer lacking valid authority.; Boundary: Contract sections 3.2–3.5 address transfer instructions and adverse claims; network consensus is not that authorization.; Status: documented
    Sources: Securitize July 2026 S-1 (2026-07-31) · Securitize live Wormhole deployment (2025-01-28) · BUIDL platform, transfer agent and registrar agreement (2024-03-14) · Securitize, LLC transfer-agent filing (2025-03-03) · BUIDL Solana launch and seven-network availability (2025-03-25)

    USDC · issue, transfer and redeem

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: USDC
    Description
    Follow the token, reserve money and issuer records. Direct redemption depends on customer eligibility; token movement does not prove bank payout.
    Stages
    • Title: Mint access and eligibility · Lanes: Asset: Text: Circle Mint provides the access path for an eligible institution to seek issuance of USDC.; Boundary: KYC and service access are mapped; a particular bank-funding instruction and posting receipt are absent.; Status: documented; Money: Text: A specific incoming USD payment route or settlement receipt is not mapped.; Boundary: Access eligibility does not prove bank funding, reserve receipt, or final settlement of a given order.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: The applicable legal issuer is the issuer-side liability and instruction authority for USDC.; Boundary: The issuer perimeter remains distinct from Circle Mint access and from every supported network.; Status: documented
    • Title: Reserve and native mint · Lanes: Asset: Text: Native USDC is minted under issuer instruction on a selected supported chain.; Boundary: This generic trace does not specify the selected-chain execution for a particular issuance.; Status: documented; Money: Text: Dollar assets enter an issuer-specific segregated reserve pool.; Boundary: The reserve-pool role is mapped, not a transaction-level reserve inflow posting.; Status: documented; Record: Text: The issuer's USDC obligation and reserve records remain separate from token state.; Boundary: Chain state does not itself establish the issuer liability or reserve position.; Status: documented
    • Title: Token transport · Lanes: Asset: Text: USDC can move through wallets and supported transport mechanisms.; Boundary: The mechanisms are alternatives, not successive mandatory hops in one transaction.; Status: documented; Money: Text: No token transfer alone establishes an FX conversion, bank payout, or new fiat settlement.; Boundary: Token transport is not evidence of completed money movement outside the issuer claim.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Technical token state and transport are distinct from the issuer liability record and redemption eligibility.; Boundary: Chain finality does not guarantee direct Circle redemption eligibility.; Status: documented
    • Title: Redemption and bank payout · Lanes: Asset: Text: USDC is burned under applicable issuer eligibility rules when redeemed.; Boundary: No transaction-specific burn receipt is supplied.; Status: documented; Money: Text: Reserve liquidity is intended to become bank USD payout, but a separate direct-Circle payout completion card is not mapped.; Boundary: Do not use a distinct Tazapay conversion/local-payout route to fill this direct-redemption gap.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Issuer redemption terms govern the obligation; token burn and bank payout remain distinct evidence points.; Boundary: Burn does not by itself prove completed bank payout or discharge for a specific customer.; Status: documented
    Sources: USDC and Circle Mint (2026-09-01) · USDC Terms (2026-09-01) · Circle Mint supported chains and currencies (2026-09-02) · USDC reserve transparency (2026-09-01)

    Coinbase certificate · underlying share to registered title

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03
    Description
    Follow the underlying share, issued certificate and controlling register. Wallet possession and registered ownership are distinct.
    Stages
    • Title: Creation admission · Lanes: Asset: Text: An Authorized Participant submits the current in-kind creation order for the certificate process.; Boundary: Eligibility is mapped, but acceptance of a particular in-kind creation instruction lacks a dedicated card.; Status: documented; Money: Text: This is an in-kind underlying-security creation case; no cash payment route is mapped.; Boundary: The saved trace does not establish a cash-leg settlement for an individual creation.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Certificate eligibility and later vesting gates are distinct from wallet possession.; Boundary: Admission does not itself establish registered ownership.; Status: documented
    • Title: Underlying custody and certificate issuance · Lanes: Asset: Text: AAPL enters the issuer-named Alpaca custody account; Coinbase Onchain SPV holds deposited property on trust and legally issues the certificate.; Boundary: The certificate is not direct ownership of the underlying U.S. share, and the underlying company does not sponsor it.; Status: documented; Money: Text: No cash purchase, securities-loan, or cash-settlement instruction is documented for this stage.; Boundary: Custody and certificate issuance do not prove a separate cash leg.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: The SPV-issued certificate is a distinct legal object against deposited underlying property.; Boundary: Underlying custody is separate from certificate issuance, wallet possession, and Base state.; Status: documented
    • Title: Base representation and vesting · Lanes: Asset: Text: The B20 certificate is represented on Base.; Boundary: Legal issuance and Base representation are mapped; the OML-specific mint action is not separately recorded.; Status: documented; Money: Text: Base transaction ordering and Ethereum settlement do not identify a cash settlement.; Boundary: Sequencer ordering and Ethereum finality do not determine certificate cash settlement.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: Wallet control creates an onchain position, while OML separately applies eligibility and vesting checks.; Boundary: Wallet possession alone does not establish registered title.; Status: documented
    • Title: Legal Register finality and servicing · Lanes: Asset: Text: Certificate rights, including redemption and voting eligibility, depend on registered and vested status.; Boundary: Unvested holders lack the documented redemption and voting rights.; Status: documented; Money: Text: A cash redemption or payout route is not established by the certificate or its Base representation.; Boundary: The trace does not supply a dedicated redemption/burn execution or cash-settlement action.; Status: unresolved; Record: Text: OML operates the definitive Legal Register; registered entry and vesting determine certificate title.; Boundary: The Legal Register, rather than Base state or wallet possession alone, controls title and servicing.; Status: documented
    Sources: Coinbase Onchain SPV AAPL prospectus (2026) · Coinbase Tokenize (2026-09-01) · Base protocol and sequencer terms (2026-09-01)

    Question 12026-10-0149Adviser self-custodyPursuant to the proposed adviser self-custody rule, an adviser would be permitted to have self-custody of a client’s crypto asset without maintaining it at a qualified custodian, provided that the adviser complies with the requirements of the proposed adviser self-custody rule. Should an adviser be permitted to have self-custody of client crypto assets, including crypto assets of a regulated fund, as proposed? Why or why not?SEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules proposal (the home's own source) · SEC crypto-custody rulemaking page (the home's own source) · What does the SEC custody proposal ask commenters, topic by topic?
    Question 22026-10-0149Adviser self-custodyDo commenters agree that qualified custodian availability is a particularly acute problem for certain kinds of crypto assets, such as nascent or novel crypto assets? If so, what types of crypto assets raise heightened challenges to finding available qualified custodians to maintain them? To what extent would the proposed rule permitting crypto asset custody at State trust companies discussed below (see section II.C) alleviate these challenges?state trustSEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules proposal (the home's own source) · SEC crypto-custody rulemaking page (the home's own source) · What does the SEC custody proposal ask commenters, topic by topic?
    Question 32026-10-0149Adviser self-custodyThe Advisers Act custody rule excepts securities that meet the description of privately offered securities from the qualified custodian requirement on the basis that they are hard to steal. 124 Privately offered securities are securities that are: (i) acquired from the issuer in a transaction or chain of transactions not involving any public offering; (ii) uncertificated, and ownership thereof is recorded only on the books of the issuer or its transfer agent in the name of the client; and (iii) transferable only with prior consent of the issuer or holders of the outstanding securities of the issuer. Crypto assets would not be able to meet this exception if, for example, records of their ownership are not recorded only on the books of the issuer or its transfer agent in the name of the client, or if they can be transferred without the prior consent of the issuer. Are there crypto assets that could qualify as privately offered securities? If so, what characteristics of such crypto assets and/or their crypto networks satisfy the conditions of the privately offered securities exception? If there are crypto assets that could qualify as privately offered securities, should the privately offered securities exception be amended to except the adviser from the conditions of the proposed adviser self-custody rule with respect to any such crypto assets in the adviser’s self- custody? Why or why not? If yes, how should the privately offered securities exception be amended, if at all, to accommodate characteristics unique to securities that are crypto assets and what conditions should apply to such crypto assets under the exception to ensure that the privately offered securities exception continues to exempt only those crypto assets that have features similar to privately offered securities that provide external safeguards against the kinds of abuse the custody rule seeks to prevent?onchain recordSEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules proposal (the home's own source) · SEC crypto-custody rulemaking page (the home's own source) · What does the SEC custody proposal ask commenters, topic by topic?
    Question 42026-10-0150Adviser self-custodyIs our understanding correct that some advisers engage in extensive due diligence of a crypto asset beginning in its early stage development, and that such advisers may acquire expertise on the functioning and operation of the associated crypto network, potentially allowing them to be well-positioned to securely self-custody the crypto asset? If not, why not? How does the adviser’s due diligence of the crypto asset position the adviser to be better situated than a traditional custodian to custody the crypto asset? Does the adviser’s involvement via the due diligence of the crypto asset create or enhance any conflicts of interest that the proposed custody rule amendments should uniquely address?onchain recordSEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules proposal (the home's own source) · SEC crypto-custody rulemaking page (the home's own source) · What does the SEC custody proposal ask commenters, topic by topic?

    Question 82026-10-0156Adviser self-custodyAre the terms and definitions proposed in connection with the proposed adviser self- custody rule (“crypto network,” “crypto asset,” “crypto asset address,” “key materials,” “self-custody” and “distributed crypto asset”) clear?     Question 112026-10-0157Adviser self-custodyAs noted above, the proposed Advisers Act custody rule would continue to apply to client assets that are funds or securities (and would be amended to apply to securities and similar investments held for the accounts of regulated funds that are subject to the proposed adviser self-custody rule), and we express our view that tokenized deposits and payment stablecoins issued by stablecoin issuers that are permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act and foreign payment stablecoin issuers registered pursuant to section 18 of the GENIUS Act are crypto assets that are digital representations of funds subject to the Advisers Act custody rule. Are there other types of crypto assets, if any, that need clarification as to whether they are digital representations of “funds” subject to the Advisers Act custody rule, and why?SEC Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules proposal (the home's own source) · SEC crypto-custody rulemaking page (the home's own source) · What does the SEC custody proposal ask commenters, topic by topic?

    6 · The SEC's Innovation Exemption for tokenized stocks (Release 34-106402)

    What the order allows: the two exemptions

    · 3 rows

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenized NMS Stock Innovation Exemption 2026-09-17/INNOVATION_EXEMPTION_HUB_DATA_2026-09-17.json › exemptions

    SEC Innovation Exemption HubIn effect

    Effective: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Rule status
    Short title
    Innovation Exemption
    Release
    Exchange Act Release No. 34-106402
    File number
    4-927
    Authority
    Exchange Act section 36(a)(1)
    Effective
    2026-09-17
    Expires
    2031-09-17
    Evidence cutoff
    2026-09-17 09:46 EDT
    Source pages
    60
    Summary
    One temporary Commission order, two statutory-definition exemptions, twelve TSV condition modules, a separate Covered Firm lane, and thirty required public-notice fields.
    Boundary
    The order creates a legally available lane. It does not establish an operating TSV, select a token or chain, authorize issuance, or decide custody, transfer agency, clearing, cash, legal settlement finality, correction, or loss allocation.
    Asset rules
    • Required: Every eligible pair contains at least one Tokenized NMS Stock.
    • Pair legs: Another Tokenized NMS Stock, A non-security crypto asset, A tokenized money market fund
    • Stock models: Tokenized by or on behalf of the issuer, Tokenized by an unaffiliated third party after issuer notice and no timely objection
    • Excluded: Synthetic exposure, Tokenized linked security, Tokenized security-based swap, Rights, Warrants, Primary issuance or initial offering on the TSV
    • Tier caps (2):
    • — Tier: Tier 1; Universe: S&P 500, Russell 1000 and qualifying LULD ETPs; Symbols: 75; Volume: 0.25% of prior-month ADV
    • — Tier: Tier 2; Universe: Other eligible NMS stocks; Symbols: 250; Volume: 2.5% of prior-month ADV
    Sources: Controlling order (the home's own source)

    TSV Exemption

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: What does the SEC's tokenized-stock exemption allow, and how big can it get?
    Statutory definition
    Exchange Act §3(a)(1) — exchange
    Beneficiary
    Qualifying U.S.-person Tokenized Securities Venue
    Effect
    The qualifying TSV is exempt from the definition of exchange for activity performed through its qualifying TSV systems and functionalities.
    Scope
    Permissioned trading of Tokenized NMS Stock through qualifying AMM Liquidity Pools on public, permissionless DLT.
    Outside
    • Securities activity outside the TSV
    • Participant registration status
    • Securities Act registration or exemption
    • Antifraud and antimanipulation law
    • OFAC and other applicable law
    • Investment Company Act
    • Custody, transfer-agent, clearing and settlement law
    Pages
    Order pp. 1, 12–17, 60
    Sources: Controlling order (the home's own source)

    Covered Firm Exemption

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: What does the SEC's tokenized-stock exemption allow, and how big can it get?
    Statutory definition
    Exchange Act §3(a)(5) — dealer
    Beneficiary
    Qualifying own-account liquidity provider
    Effect
    The qualifying firm is exempt from the dealer definition solely for its bounded liquidity activity in TSV-provided AMM pools.
    Scope

    Outside
    • Customer custody
    • Unrelated securities activity
    • Broker status if separately triggered
    • Antifraud and antimanipulation law
    • Any activity outside qualifying TSV pools
    • General dealer safe harbor
    Pages
    Order pp. 4, 52–57, 60

    7 · The Federal Reserve Board's GENIUS proposals (R-1899, R-1900)

    The seven gate layers (the GENIUS Stablecoin Rulebook page's reading)

    · 8 rows

    Read from: _Workspace/Indexes/masters/stablecoins.json › genius_implementing_proposals

    What the two Board proposals would set upProposed

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Summary
    The two Board proposals define a possible federal issuer operating constitution and an insured-state-member-bank application path. They regulate legal entities, claims, assets, controls, books and clocks; they do not approve a technology stack.
    About
    The GENIUS Stablecoin Rulebook page's reading of the two Federal Reserve Board proposals (the federal issuer operating rules and the insured-state-member-bank application path, docket R-1900), copied as written: 7 layers of gates (rule, effect, clock, watch), 9 clocks, a summary and the page's status word. Placed here because this file already holds the GENIUS Act's provisions (law_context) and the Board proposals implement that Act; crypto_rules.json excludes GENIUS rules by its home rule, and genius_act_milestones.json (the dated GENIUS home) was not among the files in this pass. The staged page data carried no source links, so this block is marked needs_primary_source until the Board's proposing releases are linked from genius_act_milestones.json.
    Status
    proposed
    Open questions
    • Link the two Board proposing releases (docket R-1900) and their Federal Register dates from genius_act_milestones.json.
    • Decide whether this block moves to genius_act_milestones.json when that file is next edited.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Authority and entry

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Authority and application
    Rule: Identify the issuer, supervisor and approval route. An insured state member bank would apply through its Reserve Bank to the Board for a PPSI subsidiary, with proposed 30-day completeness and 120-day decision clocks. · Effect: Makes the legal entity, parent, control chain, consortium structure and proposed business plan visible before operation. · Clock: Proposed only; no operative R-1900 filing lane or actor-specific approval is established. · Watch: Federal Register publication, final rule, application materials, complete filing, decision and conditions.
    Gate: Claim and issuer identity
    Rule: Keep a payment stablecoin, deposit, security, native crypto asset and tokenized representation legally distinct. · Effect: Prevents a shared ledger or brand from collapsing the obligor, asset class, holder right and record authority into one object. · Clock: Definition remains proposed; statutory provisions retain their own effective state. · Watch: Final definitions, foreign-issuer treatment, deposit/securities boundary and named coin terms.
    Question
    Which legal person may enter which supervisory lane?
    Summary
    Resolve issuer identity, control, parent and state/federal route before examining technology.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Issuer business

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Permitted business
    Rule: Issuance, redemption, reserve management/custody, stablecoin/key custody and related services form the core; lending and issuance as loan proceeds are prohibited, while material non-core activity generally needs permission. · Effect: Forces non-reserve assets, liabilities, affiliate businesses, gas holdings and service revenue into an explicit perimeter. · Clock: Proposed prudential boundary; no current business has been tested under the final calibration. · Watch: Final permitted-activity text and actor-specific written permissions.
    Gate: Distribution and yield
    Rule: Issuer-paid interest or yield for holding, using or retaining a stablecoin is prohibited; specified issuer-funded affiliate, service-provider and white-label paths face a rebuttable presumption. · Effect: Brings contracts, funding flows, branding and reward economics at distribution partners into the issuer perimeter. · Clock: Proposed related-party and rebuttal tests; not a final judgment on every independent reward program. · Watch: Final related-party definition, rebuttal evidence, distributor agreements and funding source.
    Question
    What may the issuer do, hold, owe and outsource?
    Summary
    Separate core stablecoin functions from lending, material non-core assets/liabilities, affiliate economics and activities requiring permission.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Backing and custody

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Reserve assets and rights
    Rule: Maintain identifiable, segregated reserves at least equal to outstanding coins at fair value; tokenized forms of specified eligible categories must preserve identical legal rights. · Effect: Attaches eligibility to the underlying claim and rights rather than to a chain, token standard or vendor. · Clock: Proposed rule; daily 5 p.m. demonstration and any published eligibility list are not yet operative. · Watch: Final asset classes, liquidity/concentration limits, Board eligibility list and named tokenized-reserve opinion.
    Gate: Custody and control
    Rule: Covered assets require segregation, protection from creditor claims, possession/control, customer-level records and sub-custodian oversight; tokenized control turns on who can transfer without custodian consent. · Effect: Makes keys, wallet authority, omnibus subledgers and sub-custodian contracts part of the prudential control plane. · Clock: Proposed custody standard; self-custody remains outside where the provider lacks control and does not hold itself out as custodian. · Watch: Final control definition, qualified custodians, sub-custodian contracts and first examined custody stack.
    Question
    What backs the claim, which rights travel through tokenization and who controls the assets?
    Summary
    Join 1:1 fair-value reserves, underlying-asset eligibility, identical rights, segregation, possession/control and sub-custodian records.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Claim lifecycle

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Supply and reconciliation
    Rule: Mint/burn authority, outstanding liability, reserve value, transaction processing, internal books and custodian records must remain reconcilable. · Effect: Treats on-chain supply as one record in a multi-record operating system, not the whole issuer balance sheet. · Clock: Application evidence and operating controls are proposed; no named stack has passed review. · Watch: Named key holders, supply controls, reconciliation frequency, breaks and examiner access.
    Gate: Distribution and yield
    Rule: Issuer-paid interest or yield for holding, using or retaining a stablecoin is prohibited; specified issuer-funded affiliate, service-provider and white-label paths face a rebuttable presumption. · Effect: Brings contracts, funding flows, branding and reward economics at distribution partners into the issuer perimeter. · Clock: Proposed related-party and rebuttal tests; not a final judgment on every independent reward program. · Watch: Final related-party definition, rebuttal evidence, distributor agreements and funding source.
    Gate: Redemption and liquidity
    Rule: Direct redemption would begin at one coin and generally finish within two business days, subject to onboarding, bounded safe harbors and regulator-imposed emergency limits. · Effect: Separates issuer redemption, reserve monetization and external wallet/exchange/bank settlement clocks. · Clock: Proposed service clock; no universal secondary-market par guarantee or end-to-end payout clock. · Watch: Final holder right, fees, onboarding, liquidity buffers, redemption incidents and cash-settlement receipts.
    Question
    How is supply created, distributed, reconciled and redeemed?
    Summary
    Connect mint/burn authority and issuer books to distribution contracts, direct redemption and external settlement.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Operations and proof

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Operational risk
    Rule: Governance must cover smart contracts, private keys, cyber, privacy, continuity, third parties, AML/CFT, sanctions, transaction processing and records. · Effect: Turns networks, oracles, bridges, wallets and vendors into accountable dependencies with change, incident and recovery controls. · Clock: Proposed controls; an enterprise parent framework does not erase PPSI-specific accountability. · Watch: Final control standards, service-provider contracts, recovery tests, incidents and supervisory findings.
    Gate: Reporting and examination
    Rule: Monthly examined reserve reports, executive certifications, confidential weekly operating data, public quarterly financials and periodic full-scope examinations would expose the operating body. · Effect: Creates distinct public, supervisory and examiner-access data planes, including access to DLT records. · Clock: Proposed reporting/exam regime; 18-to-36-month exam discretion depends on specified conditions. · Watch: Final forms, first filings, auditor criteria, examination cycle and publication quality.
    Question
    Which controls keep the system inspectable and recoverable?
    Summary
    Bind governance, smart contracts, keys, vendors, cyber, privacy, continuity, financial crime, public reports and examiner access.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Capital and loss

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Capital and loss
    Rule: Capital combines tangible equity, reserve credit-risk charges, graduated issuance scale, non-reserve revenue and a realized-loss scalar with remediation powers. · Effect: Links reserve counterparties, operating scale, service businesses and historical losses to a separate loss-absorbing buffer. · Clock: All percentages and scalar parameters remain proposed. · Watch: Final calibration, eligible capital, look-through methods, loss data and remediation orders.
    Question
    Which buffer absorbs reserve credit and operating loss?
    Summary
    Keep tangible equity, reserve credit charges, issuance scale, non-reserve revenue, loss history and remediation distinct.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Parent, state and emergency seams

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19 · Needs a primary source
    Gate: Parent, state and transition
    Rule: Parent-bank capital would deconsolidate the PPSI and deduct its minimum from CET1; state issuers retain ordinary state supervision with extraordinary Board backup and a separate large-issuer transition lane. · Effect: Separates subsidiary loss absorption, parent exposure, state supervision and emergency infrastructure failure. · Clock: Proposed capital, enforcement and transition mechanics; no state issuer is converted by this release. · Watch: Final rule, state certification/equivalence, waiver decisions, first examination and emergency action.
    Question
    Where do subsidiary, parent, state and Board responsibility meet?
    Summary
    Track parent CET1, ordinary state supervision, extraordinary Board backup, transition waivers and infrastructure-failure indicators.

    What the Fed's GENIUS proposals change in the crypto stackProposed

    Evidence cutoff: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which legal roles would surround a Board-supervised stablecoin issuer?
    Status legend
    • Label: Issuer / application interface · Meaning: The governed ecosystem contains a payment-stablecoin issuer or issuer-like operating surface that would face the proposal directly if the exact legal entity enters the Board-supervised lane. This is not an eligibility or approval finding.
    • Label: Custody / distribution interface · Meaning: The ecosystem supplies custody, distribution, market, cash or payout functions that the issuer would have to map and control, without becoming the issuer merely by providing them.
    • Label: Technical control interface · Meaning: The ecosystem can carry token state, contracts, data or interoperability and would be tested as an operational dependency, not as the legal source of issuer authority or reserve eligibility.
    • Label: Outside direct issuer perimeter · Meaning: The tracked object is primarily a different asset, market or institutional function. It may connect to the stack, but the proposal does not directly convert it into a payment-stablecoin issuer or reserve.
    Schema version
    1.0
    Subtitle
    Twenty governed ecosystems mapped against twelve proposed issuer, reserve, custody, redemption, reporting, capital and application gates.
    Evidence cutoff
    2026-09-24T15:12:00-04:00
    Status
    proposed
    Summary
    The two Board proposals define a possible federal issuer operating constitution and an insured-state-member-bank application path. They regulate legal entities, claims, assets, controls, books and clocks; they do not approve a technology stack. The matrix shows which current Hub surface would be directly tested, used as a regulated service interface, treated as a technical dependency, or remain outside the direct issuer perimeter.
    Boundary
    Every row is a proposal-overlap finding only. It does not establish that an ecosystem is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, an eligible reserve asset, an approved custodian, a Board-approved subsidiary, compliant with a final rule or operating in a Board-supervised lane.

    Authority and application

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?

    Identify the issuer, supervisor and approval route. An insured state member bank would apply through its Reserve Bank to the Board for a PPSI subsidiary, with proposed 30-day completeness and 120-day decision clocks.

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?

    Custody and control

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?
    Rule
    Covered assets require segregation, protection from creditor claims, possession/control, customer-level records and sub-custodian oversight; tokenized control turns on who can transfer without custodian consent.

    Makes keys, wallet authority, omnibus subledgers and sub-custodian contracts part of the prudential control plane.

    Capital and loss

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?
    Rule
    Capital combines tangible equity, reserve credit-risk charges, graduated issuance scale, non-reserve revenue and a realized-loss scalar with remediation powers.
    Infrastructure effect
    Links reserve counterparties, operating scale, service businesses and historical losses to a separate loss-absorbing buffer.
    Implementation clock
    All percentages and scalar parameters remain proposed.

    Final calibration, eligible capital, look-through methods, loss data and remediation orders.

    Parent, state and transition

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?
    Rule
    Parent-bank capital would deconsolidate the PPSI and deduct its minimum from CET1; state issuers retain ordinary state supervision with extraordinary Board backup and a separate large-issuer transition lane.
    Infrastructure effect
    Separates subsidiary loss absorption, parent exposure, state supervision and emergency infrastructure failure.
    Implementation clock
    Proposed capital, enforcement and transition mechanics; no state issuer is converted by this release.
    Watch
    Final rule, state certification/equivalence, waiver decisions, first examination and emergency action.

    Backup authority does not make the Board the routine primary supervisor of every state issuer.

    The legal issuer sits inside a supervised operating body

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which legal roles would surround a Board-supervised stablecoin issuer?
    Summary
    Read each lane as a different legal relationship around the same issuer. Repeated appearances of the issuer do not create multiple issuers; they show that one legal person carries several distinct obligations.
    Boundary
    This is a proposal architecture, not an organization chart for a named company. A brand, network, wallet or affiliate does not inherit the issuer's authority merely because it appears in the same commercial ecosystem.
    Sources: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations (the home's own source) (2026-09-24) · R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs (the home's own source) (2026-09-24) · R-1900 proposed insured-state-member-bank PPSI application process (the home's own source) (2026-09-24) · Statement on proposals to implement the GENIUS Act by Governor Michael S.     Federal Reserve Board

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which legal roles would surround a Board-supervised stablecoin issuer?
    Gates
    • Authority and application
    • Reporting and examination
    • Parent, state and transition
    Kind
    Federal authority
    Role
    Would issue the framework, decide the insured-state-member-bank subsidiary application and exercise the Board powers assigned by the GENIUS Act.
    Proof
    Final rules, a complete application, an approval or conditional order, examination authority and any actor-specific enforcement record.
    Boundary
    The Board is not the stablecoin issuer, reserve owner, custodian or cash-settlement bank.
