    Worked case: a Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuer

    · 1 rows

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/FED_GENIUS_INFRASTRUCTURE_CHANGE_MAP_2026-09-24.json › case

    Proposed Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuer

    Home checked through: 2026-09-24 · Also shown on: Which legal roles would surround a Board-supervised stablecoin issuer?
    Step: Name the claim
    The legal object is a fixed-value payment stablecoin claim against a named permitted issuer, kept distinct from deposits, securities and native crypto assets. Still open: Final definitions, coin terms and named issuer remain unresolved.
    Step: Draw the actor perimeter
    The proposed perimeter reaches the PPSI, control/affiliate relationships, reserve and customer-asset custodians, related distribution arrangements and critical vendors. Still open: Every exact legal entity, contract, key holder and state/federal supervisory lane still needs actor-specific proof.
    Step: Establish permission
    R-1900 would create an application, completeness, 120-day decision, denial, condition and hearing process for an insured state member bank's PPSI subsidiary. Still open: No final rule, open lane, complete application or approval exists from the proposal alone.
    Step: Identify the authoritative record
    Issuer liability/supply books, ledger state, reserve records, custodian records and financial reports would have to remain reconcilable and available to supervisors. Still open: The proposal does not choose one universal authoritative technical record or reconcile a named deployment.
    Step: Bind the instruction
    Mint/burn, key, custody and transaction-processing controls would allocate who can create, move, freeze, redeem or recover the claim and its supporting assets. Still open: Named keys, contracts, access rules, administrator powers and service agreements are deployment-specific.
    Step: Clear the obligation and assemble resources
    Eligible, segregated 1:1 reserves and a separate capital buffer would support redemption and absorb specified credit and operational risks. Still open: Final eligible assets, liquidity calibration, counterparties, capital and actual available cash remain unresolved.
    Step: Settle each leg and name finality
    The issuer would generally complete direct redemption within two business days, while reserve monetization and external cash settlement keep their own clocks. Still open: The proposal does not guarantee secondary-market par or make chain confirmation equal bank-payout finality.
    Step: Post, reconcile and service
    Monthly examined reserve reports, weekly confidential operating data, quarterly financials and periodic examination would expose the ongoing body. Still open: Final forms, first filings, auditor criteria and examination findings do not yet exist.
    Step: Repair, allocate loss and prove the result
    Capital remediation, Board enforcement, state backup enforcement, redemption limitations and parent-bank capital treatment provide proposed correction and loss-allocation tools. Still open: The package does not supply a full resolution regime, government guarantee or tested loss waterfall.
    Status
    Two Board proposals; not final or operative at the saved cutoff.
    Summary
    R-1899 proposes the operating constitution and R-1900 proposes one insured-state-member-bank application route. Together they make issuer identity, reserves, custody, redemption, records, capital and approval inspectable without approving a specific actor or stack.
    Boundary
    This worked case is a proposed legal architecture. It does not establish a current Board-approved issuer, open application lane, eligible tokenized reserve, final capital requirement or production operating receipt.
    Sources: R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs (2026-09-24) · R-1900 proposed insured-state-member-bank PPSI application process (2026-09-24) · Fed GENIUS Full-Release Reading and Infrastructure Atlas — 2026-09-24 (Read the full saved research: Fed GENIUS Full-Release Reading and Infrastructure Atlas — 2026-09-24; research notes) (2026-09-24)

    8 · Stablecoin laws around the world

    Nine jurisdictions' stablecoin laws, compared

    · 9 rows

    cat values are the page's four categories (see chapter.cats): active = law in force, enacted = enacted but not yet in force, watch = under discussion, adjacent = related payment or market law.

    European Union: stablecoins need a license as e-money or asset-backed tokensActive

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The stablecoin parts of MiCA, the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation, apply from 30 Jun 2024. The rest of MiCA applies from 30 Dec 2024.
    Currency
    EUR / referenced fiat
    Who may issue
    Only a credit institution or an electronic-money institution may issue an e-money token. Issuers of asset-referenced tokens need a separate authorization.
    What has to back it
    Duties on reserves, liquidity, keeping assets separate, custody and redemption at any time differ by token type. E-money token holders can redeem at face value. Paying interest on them is prohibited.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Crypto-asset service providers need an EU-wide authorization and follow EU-wide conduct rules.
    How it settles
    The token may move on a blockchain. Issuer redemption and bank or central-bank money settle separately, each final at its own time.
    At the store checkout
    A strong legal base for connecting services. We do not claim contactless card software (EMV) reads MiCA tokens directly.
    Currency angle
    The euro system favors one equal-value euro (monetary singleness) and regulated private claims over an unlimited token market.
    Name
    European Union
    Status
    in force
    When
    30 Jun 2024
    Lead
    Europe regulates by legal type of token. It is the clearest category-first model.
    Careful
    MiCA authorization is not a European Central Bank (ECB) guarantee, deposit insurance, or acceptance by every merchant.
    Sources: EUR-Lex — Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 · EBA — MiCA regulatory products

    United Arab Emirates: stores may accept only licensed dirham tokensActive

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The Payment Token Services Regulation of the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) has been in force since 31 Aug 2024.
    Currency
    AED / registered foreign payment tokens
    Who may issue
    A UAE company may be licensed to issue a Dirham Payment Token; a bank issues through a subsidiary or affiliate. Issuing, converting, holding and transferring foreign tokens each need their own permission.
    What has to back it
    By default, reserves are 100% cash in the same currency, held in a separate escrow account at an unrelated UAE bank. A qualifying bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the rest in short UAE government or CBUAE instruments, with extra capital and controls.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Issuing, holding and transferring, and converting tokens are separate regulated services.
    How it settles
    The wallet transfer is the customer's part. Reserve cash and redemption are separate parts, at a commercial bank or, when directed, in central-bank custody.
    At the store checkout
    This is the clearest comparison for paying in stores. An ordinary UAE merchant may accept only a licensed Dirham Payment Token. Registered foreign tokens may be used only to buy virtual assets.
    Currency angle
    The law protects the dirham's role in payments by controlling which legal tokens merchants may accept, not by controlling the contactless hardware.
    Name
    United Arab Emirates
    Status
    in force
    When
    31 Aug 2024
    Lead
    The UAE shows that legal routing and merchant permission decide stablecoin acceptance, not contactless (NFC) capability.
    Careful
    A terminal that supports contactless payment does not meet the rules on token licensing, conversion, custody, merchants or redemption.
    Sources: CBUAE — Payment Token Services Regulation · CBUAE — reserve assets · CBUAE — issuance and redemption

    United States: the GENIUS Act sets who may issue and what they must holdEnacted

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    Public Law 119-27 was signed 18 Jul 2025. Final implementing rules were due 18 Jul 2026. We found none on official final-rule pages through the 28 Jul cutoff. The latest general effective date is still 18 Jan 2027. It moves earlier only if final rules start the 120-day countdown.
    Currency
    USD
    Who may issue
    Permitted issuers are subsidiaries of insured depository institutions, federal qualified issuers, or state qualified issuers, divided by the law's federal–state split and size threshold.
    What has to back it
    Reserves must match coins one-to-one: cash, central-bank balances, insured deposits, Treasury bills of 93 days or less, qualifying repurchase agreements (repo), government money funds and related liquid government assets. Issuers report monthly. Holders get no interest and no FDIC insurance.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Wallets, card networks, processors and distributors can be separate companies from the legal issuer. A restriction on service providers starts in 2028, setting a later deadline for market access.
    How it settles
    Blockchain transfer, card-network obligation, minting and redemption, bank-deposit movement and central-bank final settlement stay separate.
    At the store checkout
    GENIUS supplies the lawful issuer and reserves that a card, wallet or merchant processor (acquirer) can route. It does not update any terminal.
    Currency angle
    The reserve rules directly create demand for short-term Treasury bills. The dollar stays the unit, and private companies still distribute the coins.
    Name
    United States
    Status
    enacted · not yet generally in effect
    When
    18 Jul 2025
    Lead
    Of these laws, GENIUS most directly links more stablecoins to more government-debt purchases for reserves. It also shows most clearly that stablecoin law is banking law too.
    Careful
    Enacted does not mean in effect. A proposal, a charter application or a conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is not a live GENIUS issuer authorization.
    Sources: Congress — Public Law 119-27 · OCC — 2026 proposed issuances · OCC — 2026 final issuances

    Hong Kong: issuing a stablecoin requires a license from the Hong Kong Monetary AuthorityActive

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The Stablecoins Ordinance and the supervisory framework of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) took effect 1 Aug 2025.
    Currency
    HKD / referenced fiat
    Who may issue
    Issuing an in-scope stablecoin tied to a government currency (fiat-referenced) in Hong Kong requires a license. So do specified issuing or offering activities linked to Hong Kong.
    What has to back it
    HKMA supervision focuses on reserve management, redemption, risk management, governance, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing (AML/CFT) controls, and disclosure.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Only specified regulated institutions may offer in-scope stablecoins to retail investors. The issuer's license and the permission to distribute are separate.
    How it settles
    The Ordinance covers the issuer and the token's promise, not the merchant's card processor (acquirer) or the final bank-money payment.
    At the store checkout
    A licensed stablecoin can fund or settle payments behind an existing wallet or card. The legal link still needs an authorized distributor and processor.
    Currency angle
    Hong Kong protects its monetary system by licensing issuers and supervising them locally. It does not treat every token as bank money.
    Name
    Hong Kong
    Status
    in force
    When
    1 Aug 2025
    Lead
    Hong Kong uses licensing by the regulator: a strict issuer license in an international financial center.
    Careful
    A sandbox place, a license application or a public announcement is not a license.
    Sources: HKMA — stablecoin issuer framework · HKMA — supervision guideline

    United Kingdom: issuing stablecoins becomes a licensed activity; the full regime is expected to start in late 2027Enacted

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The 2026 cryptoasset regulations make issuing and safeguarding regulated activities. The wider regime is expected to begin in late 2027. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) still has to make rules and set application steps.
    Currency
    GBP / qualifying referenced fiat
    Who may issue
    Issuing a UK qualifying stablecoin becomes a regulated activity. For systemic payment stablecoins, the Bank of England adds oversight to FCA supervision.
    What has to back it
    Qualifying stablecoins are tied to a government currency and hold backing assets. Detailed FCA rules are expected to provide full backing and redemption rights.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Safeguarding and other crypto activities need separate permissions. The government is still settling what the dealing and payment-services rules cover.
    How it settles
    The UK is explicitly designing stablecoins as both cryptoassets and possible payment instruments, with separate oversight of systemic ones.
    At the store checkout
    Promising law for connecting services, but the payment-services rules are not finished.
    Currency angle
    The UK goes in order: what the law covers first, payments integration second, tax treatment third.
    Name
    United Kingdom
    Status
    law made · regime scheduled
    When
    Feb 2026
    Lead
    Britain is the best example of a license requirement already in law whose operating rules are still being written.
    Careful
    Do not call the late-2027 regime live. Current policy notes explicitly describe more rules and payments reform still to come.
    Sources: HM Treasury — cryptoasset regime · HM Treasury — April 2026 stablecoin payments note · HMRC — stablecoin tax treatment

    South Korea: a bank-led won stablecoin is under discussion, not lawWatch

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The Digital Asset Committee of Korea's Financial Services Commission (FSC) discussed the government review draft. Legislation and the final design for issuers are not settled.
    Currency
    KRW
    Who may issue
    A bank-centered model, including a debated consortium with banks holding 50%+1, was discussed, not adopted.
    What has to back it
    Not final.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Not final. Existing bank-token and wholesale-settlement pilots are separate from any won-stablecoin law.
    How it settles
    The Bank of Korea's work puts central-bank and commercial-bank money first, with stablecoins as a supplementary option.
    At the store checkout
    Korea runs advanced payment and token pilots, but they have not led to an enacted law for paying merchants directly in stablecoins.
    Currency angle
    What institutions are actually working on is tokenizing bank deposits and testing wholesale settlement. The rules for stablecoin issuers remain open.
    Name
    South Korea
    Status
    under policy discussion · not enacted
    When
    4 Mar 2026
    Lead
    Korea is the comparison case: strong technical readiness does not mean settled law.
    Careful
    A committee discussion or a bank proof of concept is not a won-stablecoin law.
    Sources: FSC — Digital Asset Committee, 4 Mar 2026

    Japan: trust-issued stablecoins may hold up to half their reserves in short government bondsActive

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    Japan's 2022 rules for electronic payment instruments (EPIs) have applied since 1 Jun 2023. The main parts of Act No. 66 of 2025 and its final implementing rules took effect 1 Jun 2026.
    Currency
    JPY / qualifying referenced fiat
    Who may issue
    Banks, registered funds-transfer providers, and trust companies or trust banks issue different legal claims. A lighter intermediary that holds no customer assets may broker for a full provider.
    What has to back it
    Covered trust stablecoins may hold up to 50% in qualifying government bonds of three months or less, or in term deposits that can be withdrawn early without losing principal. At least 50% stays in demand deposits. Rules on daily fair-value measurement and fixing shortfalls apply.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Full EPI providers handle sale, exchange, brokering or custody. The lighter intermediary cannot hold customer assets.
    How it settles
    Trust redemption, deposit-token settlement, bank reserves and a public-blockchain transfer are different things. Each settles on its own timeline.
    At the store checkout
    Japan is setting the legal roles for issuers, intermediaries and redemption. A payment service provider could keep the tap while changing funding or payout behind it.
    Currency angle
    Yen Currency Watch grades for stability and payment use: underlying order B; exchange order B; current-payment usability A; systemic service A. The yen is absorbing the change in an orderly way, not showing a broken payment system.
    Name
    Japan
    Status
    in force
    When
    1 Jun 2026
    Lead
    Like GENIUS, Japan lets reserves fund government debt, but more narrowly: only trust stablecoins may hold limited short government bonds.
    Careful
    JPYSC running on controlled venues is not open-wallet circulation at merchants. Tokenized bank deposits are not trust stablecoins.
    Sources: FSA — final implementing package, 22 May 2026 · FSA — 2025 bill overview · FSA — stablecoin Q&A

    Japan: crypto trading moves under securities law; stablecoins stay under payments lawAdjacent

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The Diet (Japan's parliament) passed the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (FIEA) and Payment Services Act (PSA) reform 15 Jul 2026. Its main parts start on a Cabinet-set date within the legal window.
    Currency
    Crypto market perimeter
    Who may issue
    This is not a new stablecoin issuer category. Stablecoins, as electronic payment instruments, stay under the PSA.
    What has to back it
    This card covers no change to stablecoin reserves.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Rules on trading, offerings, lending, management, advice, disclosure, intermediary duties and unfair trading move under the FIEA.
    How it settles
    The law deliberately keeps market regulation separate from the settlement of payment money.
    At the store checkout
    The law helps institutions classify crypto investment activity. It does not make crypto a means of contactless payment.
    Currency angle
    Japan is building two legal paths: payments law for money claims that can be redeemed, and market law for cryptoassets held as investments.
    Name
    Japan
    Status
    enacted · not yet in effect
    When
    15 Jul 2026
    Lead
    The split is the key point. Japan keeps ‘crypto,’ ‘stablecoin’ and ‘bank deposit’ as separate legal things.
    Careful
    Do not say Japan made every cryptoasset a security, legal tender or a bank deposit.
    Sources: FSA — Diet bills · FSA — 2026 reform overview

    Japan: paper checks and bills to stop clearing from April 2027 (a plan, not a stablecoin law)Adjacent

    Home checked through: 2026-07-28 · Also shown on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
    When
    The plan aims for zero paper bills and checks through the electronic clearinghouse by the end of FY2026, and an end to paper exchange from the start of FY2027.
    Currency
    JPY bank payments
    Who may issue
    Banks still owe the payment; only the form of the payment instruction changes.
    What has to back it
    No stablecoin reserve rule applies.
    Who may sell or hold it for you
    Electronically recorded monetary claims and internet transfers replace presenting paper.
    How it settles
    This is a direct move from cash and checks to electronic payment systems, separate from stablecoin law.
    At the store checkout
    It is the closest historical parallel in this set: the paper instrument disappears while the bank relationship stays.
    Currency angle
    A mature currency system can retire an old payment instrument without changing the unit of account.
    Name
    Japan
    Status
    official transition plan from industry and government
    When
    FY2027 start
    Lead
    Japan is changing both ends at once. It is retiring paper claims while making new tokenized claims legal.
    Careful
    This is an official transition plan. It is not a stablecoin law, and it does not prove every check disappears on one day.
    Sources: FSA — bills and checks transition

    What is uncertain

    • Primary sources only: official records (Congress, agencies, courts, the Federal Register) and the actor's own documents. No news, blogs or law-firm summaries.
    • Every row remains not selected and not operating under Release 34-106402. Core candidate means architectural overlap only; it does not establish legal qualification, integration, issuer acceptance, a TSV notice, an eligible pool or observed trading.
    • Every row is a proposal-overlap finding only. It does not establish that an ecosystem is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, an eligible reserve asset, an approved custodian, a Board-approved subsidiary, compliant with a final rule or operating in a Board-supervised lane.
    • The Board's GENIUS proposal reading in stablecoins.json is marked needs_primary_source (the two proposing releases are not yet linked); its rows carry that label.
    • The stablecoin-law cards date from July 28, 2026; laws may have moved since. Each card keeps its own status.
    • No crypto master in this workbench carries a machine-readable conflict file; the conflict logs the masters cite (masters/conflicts/*_CONFLICTS.md) are not in this workbench, so no crypto conflict could be shown with both readings.

    • Masters: genius_act_milestones.json, crypto_rules.json, stablecoins.json (law_context, genius_implementing_proposals), stablecoin_laws.json.
